text:
zane: Heads-up — I noticed a hole in token-level latency for the /generate route after the canary kernel selector flip. Lots of per-token metrics show 0 or dropouts between 15:02 and 15:07 UTC. Suspect exporter tag change (kernel/selector) so dashboards lost slices.

mia: Which exporter are you seeing missing slices from — StatsD or OTel? I rolled selector-3 in canary at 15:00, it switches kernel_tag -> kernel_selector label.

zane: monitoring-bot is showing gaps in both the statsd-derived dashboards and the OTLP ingestion. Example from the quick query: `sum(token_latency_ms{route="/generate",kernel==""})` returned a bunch of empty-tag buckets.

monitoring-bot: automated note: detected metric label churn for metric "token_latency_ms" on hosts: gpu-pool-canary-* between 1819000800-1819001000 (count: 1248). Possible tag rename: kernel -> kernel_selector. See sample payload: ```statsd: token_latency_ms: 0|ms|#route:/generate,kernel_selector:selector-3```

raj: Likely cause: statsd-exporter/otlp pipeline didn't map the new kernel_selector label to the legacy kernel tag used by dashboards. We had partial mapping logic in the pipeline that only handled kernel/* values. When selector-3 emits kernel_selector instead, aggregation keys change = new timeseries.

clare: Agreed. Short term we should backfill the missing series into graphite/Prom and run a one-off re-aggregation so SLO alerts don't fire. Long term we need a compatibility layer in the statsd->OTel transform and a test that rejects label churn.

mia: Quick triage steps I ran: 
- Verified canary config: selector-3 uses kernel_selector label.
- Pulled a sample trace from kvcache hotpath, kernel name present in `attributes.kernel` but different key in metrics.
- Local fix: patch statsd-exporter to copy kernel_selector -> kernel until dashboards updated. Patch: ```diff
--- exporter/config.go
+++ exporter/config.go
@@ -120,6 +120,10 @@ func normalizeTags(tags map[string]string) map[string]string {
     if v, ok := tags["kernel_selector"]; ok {
+        // backfill compatibility: duplicate into legacy "kernel" key
+        tags["kernel"] = v
     }
+    // end compatibility backfill
     return tags
 }
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: statsd-exporter/compat-backfill patch queued for canary, CI ok, rollout at 15:45 UTC. :rocket:

zane: Thanks. For the backfill job itself — raj/clare, can you coordinate a PromQL/TSDB re-ingest? We need per-route KPIs (p50/p95 per-token) restored for 15:00-15:10 window. Also add an annotation in the dashboard about the selector change.

raj: Will run a backfill job that maps kernel_selector->kernel for the affected timestamp range and re-computes the token-level histograms into their per-token buckets. Plan: 
1) export raw OTLP batch for gpu-pool-canary hosts (s3://redwood-metrics/otlp/canary/1819000*)
2) run transform script to remap label and reformat to Prom write format
3) use promtool tsdb rewrite or remote-write to a backfill target
I can kick step 1 now.

clare: I'll mute related SLO alerts and add a temporary dashboard filter to show both kernel and kernel_selector until data is stable. Also adding a postmortem checklist item: enforce stable metric key names in rollout playbooks.

mia: One more note — we should add a unit test in the selector change PR that asserts the exported metric labels are stable across rollout modes (legacy, selector-3). I can add it to the runtime test harness: sample-metrics -> assert label set includes "kernel".

zane: Good. After backfill completes, can someone post the Prom query and a screenshot link? I want to sanity-check token-level p95 deltas pre/post.

monitoring-bot: Backfill job started by raj at 15:27 UTC. Job id: fb-9021. Estimated time 8m. Will post success/failure.

raj: Step 1 done, exported ~1.2M samples to s3://redwood-metrics/otlp/canary/1819005432-1819005630.ndjson. Starting transform now.

clare: Alerts muted. Dashboard note added: "15:00 UTC canary selector label change — backfill in progress".

ops-bot: deploy-bot: statsd-exporter compat-backfill rolled to canary at 15:46 UTC, no regressions observed.

zane: Nice work. After this, let's add a lint rule in infra that blocks label renames without a migration plan. I can draft the PR and ping product. :+1:
